title: Carboxylic acids
keyIdea: Carboxylic acids contain the –COOH group: methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic and butanoic acid have 1 to 4 carbons, counting the carbon in –COOH. Only the hydrogen on the oxygen can leave as H⁺, and only a small fraction of molecules do so at any moment, so they are weak acids. They react with metals to give a salt and hydrogen, with carbonates to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide, and with alcohols to make esters.

kid: Vinegar tastes sharp because it has ethanoic acid in it. Ethanoic acid is one of a family called carboxylic acids.
Each one ends in a group of atoms written COOH. One carbon, two oxygens and a hydrogen. The carbon in that group counts when you name the acid. Ethanoic acid has two carbons in all.

Only one hydrogen can come off, the one stuck to an oxygen. And in water, only about one molecule in a hundred lets it go. So vinegar is a weak acid. It still fizzes with baking soda, but more gently than a strong acid.
Mix an acid like this with an alcohol and a drop of strong acid, then warm it. You get an ester and water. Many esters smell of fruit, like pear drops or bananas.
adult: The functional group is the carboxyl group, –COOH: a carbon with a C=O double bond and an O–H. Names use the alkane stem for the total number of carbons, including the carboxyl carbon, plus '-oic acid': methanoic HCOOH, ethanoic CH₃COOH, propanoic CH₃CH₂COOH, butanoic CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH.

In water the O–H hydrogen ionises reversibly: CH₃COOH ⇌ CH₃COO⁻ + H⁺. At 0.1 mol/dm³ only about 1% of ethanoic acid molecules are ionised, so the pH is about 2.9, compared with about 1 for hydrochloric acid at the same concentration. That is what 'weak' means: partly ionised, not dilute.

They show typical acid reactions, only more slowly. With magnesium: 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂. With sodium carbonate: 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂, which turns limewater milky. The salts are named '-oate', such as sodium ethanoate. With enough time, a weak acid releases as much hydrogen as a strong one of the same concentration and volume, because molecules keep ionising as H⁺ is used up.

With an alcohol, warmed with a concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst, a carboxylic acid forms an ester and water. The name puts the alcohol part first and the acid part second: ethanol + ethanoic acid → ethyl ethanoate. Common mistakes: forgetting to count the carboxyl carbon, thinking all four hydrogens in ethanoic acid are acidic, confusing weak with dilute, and writing the ester name the wrong way round.

familyTip: Put a spoon of baking soda in a glass and add vinegar. Then repeat with the vinegar mixed half and half with water. Both fizz, but which is faster? Talk about why a weak acid still fizzes.

worked.title: Name the ester made from propanol and ethanoic acid, and give its formula.
steps: The alcohol gives the first word. Propanol has 3 carbons, so it becomes 'propyl'.
The acid gives the second word. Ethanoic acid becomes 'ethanoate'.
So the ester is propyl ethanoate.
The acid part CH₃COO– joins to the alcohol chain –CH₂CH₂CH₃: CH₃COOCH₂CH₂CH₃. The O–H from the acid and the H from the alcohol's O–H leave as water.

practice.hint: Count every carbon, including the one in –COOH.
practice.explain: There are three carbons, CH₃, CH₂ and the carboxyl carbon, so it is propanoic acid. Propanol is the alcohol with –OH.

practice.prompt: Ethanoic acid is added to sodium carbonate. Which gas is given off?
practice.hint: Which gas does any acid give with a carbonate?
practice.explain: Acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide. The gas turns limewater milky; the salt is sodium ethanoate.

practice.prompt: A carboxylic acid has {n} carbon atoms in total. How many hydrogen atoms are in one molecule?
practice.hint: Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, has 2 carbons and 4 hydrogens. The general formula is CₙH₂ₙO₂.
practice.explain: Carboxylic acids fit CₙH₂ₙO₂, so {n} carbons means 2 × {n} = {=2*n} hydrogens. Only one of them, the O–H hydrogen, is acidic.

practice.prompt: Why is ethanoic acid called a weak acid?
choices: It is always diluted with water
Only a small fraction of its molecules ionise to give H⁺
It has only one hydrogen atom
practice.hint: Weak and dilute are not the same idea.
practice.explain: Weak means partly ionised: at 0.1 mol/dm³ about 1 in 100 molecules release H⁺. Dilute means little acid per volume.

practice.prompt: In 2CH₃COOH + Na₂CO₃ → 2CH₃COONa + H₂O + CO₂, how many molecules of ethanoic acid react with {n} formula units of sodium carbonate?
practice.hint: Compare the numbers in front of CH₃COOH and Na₂CO₃.
practice.explain: Two ethanoic acid molecules react per Na₂CO₃, so {n} units need 2 × {n} = {=2*n} molecules.

pool.prompt: Which ester forms from methanol and butanoic acid?
pool.hint: The alcohol gives the '-yl' word, the acid gives the '-oate' word.
pool.explain: Methanol becomes 'methyl' and butanoic acid becomes 'butanoate': methyl butanoate, CH₃CH₂CH₂COOCH₃.

pool.prompt: In ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, which hydrogen is released as H⁺ in water?
choices: any of the three on the CH₃
pool.hint: Which bond breaks to leave a negative ion with the charge on oxygen?
pool.explain: Only the O–H hydrogen ionises, leaving the ethanoate ion CH₃COO⁻. C–H bonds do not break in water.

pool.prompt: Hydrochloric acid and ethanoic acid are both 0.1 mol/dm³. Which statement is true?
choices: They have the same pH because the concentration is the same
Ethanoic acid has the higher pH because fewer of its molecules ionise
Ethanoic acid has the lower pH because its molecules are bigger
pool.hint: pH depends on how many H⁺ ions are in solution.
pool.explain: HCl is fully ionised (pH about 1). Only about 1% of ethanoic acid ionises, so there is less H⁺ and the pH is about 2.9.

pool.prompt: Magnesium is added to propanoic acid. What are the products?
choices: magnesium propanoate, water and carbon dioxide
pool.hint: Metal + acid → salt + which gas? Only carbonates make carbon dioxide.
pool.explain: A metal and an acid give a salt and hydrogen. The salt of propanoic acid is a propanoate.

pool.prompt: How many carbon atoms are in one molecule of the ester made from {a}-carbon alcohol and a {b}-carbon carboxylic acid?
pool.hint: All the carbons from both molecules stay in the ester; only water leaves.
pool.explain: Water (H₂O) holds no carbon, so the ester keeps {a} + {b} = {=a+b} carbons.

pool.hint: How many carbons are there in total?
pool.explain: HCOOH has one carbon, the carboxyl carbon itself, so it is methanoic acid.

pool.prompt: What else is needed to make ethyl ethanoate from ethanol and ethanoic acid at a useful rate?
choices: a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid, and warming
pool.hint: Esterification is slow and needs a catalyst.
pool.explain: Concentrated sulfuric acid catalyses the reaction, and warming speeds it up. Ester and water form.

pool.prompt: With excess magnesium, {=2*k} molecules of ethanoic acid react completely: 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂. How many hydrogen molecules form?
pool.hint: Two acid molecules give one H₂.
pool.explain: Two molecules of acid give one H₂, so {=2*k} molecules give {=2*k} ÷ 2 = {k} molecules of hydrogen. A weak acid gives the same total in the end, just more slowly.

pool.prompt: Which is the displayed group that makes a molecule a carboxylic acid?
choices: –COOH: C=O and O–H on the same carbon
pool.explain: The carboxyl group has a carbon double-bonded to one oxygen and single-bonded to an O–H.

visual.caption: Which family is each molecule in? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: stretch the chain to name the acid, find the hydrogen that leaves, race magnesium in a strong and a weak acid, and make esters.
